name: CQL
summary: Offline RL fails because bootstrapped Q-values are wildly overestimated for out-of-distribution actions the dataset never contains. CQL adds a regularizer that pushes down Q-values for unseen actions while pushing up values for dataset actions, yielding a conservative lower bound on true value. It became the reference algorithm for extracting policies from logged robot data.
innovation: Explicit pessimism about out-of-distribution actions as a principled fix for offline value overestimation.
Made large static robot datasets usable for RL rather than only for imitation.
matters: The bridge between the field's growing demonstration datasets and reward-driven improvement.
limits: Conservatism costs performance when the dataset is broad; tuning the penalty is delicate.
lineage: A pessimistic variant of the off-policy actor-critic family SAC established.
